title: Finite-index transfer on continuous cochain complexes
statement:
Let $E$ be a topological field [def-weil-field], $G$ a profinite group, $H\subseteq G$ an open subgroup, and $V$ a topological $E$-vector space with continuous $E$-linear $G$-action. For a topological group $J$ and a topological $E$-vector space $V$ with continuous linear $J$-action define the ordinary nonnegative complex $C^n_{\mathrm{cts}}(J,V)=C(J^n,V)$ of abstract $E$-vector spaces, with $C^0_{\mathrm{cts}}(J,V)=V$ and differential
$$(df)(g_1,\ldots,g_{n+1})=g_1f(g_2,\ldots,g_{n+1})+\sum_{i=1}^n(-1)^if(g_1,\ldots,g_ig_{i+1},\ldots,g_{n+1})+(-1)^{n+1}f(g_1,\ldots,g_n).$$
For $n=0$ this reads $(dv)(g)=gv-v$. Cohomology means kernel modulo image in abstract $E$-vector spaces, with no closure of the coboundaries. Restriction is the cochain map $\mathrm{res}:C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,V)\to C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cts}}(H,V)$. There exists an $E$-linear cochain map
$$\mathrm{cor}:C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cts}}(H,V)\longrightarrow C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cts}}(G,V)$$
whose composite $\mathrm{cor}\,\mathrm{res}$ is cochain-homotopic to $[G:H]\,\mathrm{id}$. The homotopy consists of $E$-linear maps between these spaces of continuous functions. The construction can be made simultaneously natural in continuous $G$-equivariant $E$-linear maps of coefficient spaces: such maps commute with $\mathrm{cor}$ and with the homotopy. Thus a closed $G$-stable coefficient subspace is preserved by transfer when the transfer is constructed for it and for $V$ using the same coset representatives. No completeness or local compactness of $V$ and no discreteness of its topology are required.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-topological-homogeneous-cochain-coordinates] for $J=G$ and $J=H$ with the restricted coefficient action. Denote its homogeneous complexes by $B_G,B_H$ and its coordinate maps by $\Phi_J,\Psi_J$. Their differentials are alternating deletion, and restriction of functions $R:B_G\to B_H$ corresponds exactly to the restriction in the item, by the stated restriction compatibility. It suffices to construct transfer $T:B_H\to B_G$ and a homotopy $K$ with $\delta K+K\delta=TR-[G:H]\,\mathrm{id}$: conjugation by the stated cochain isomorphisms then gives the required maps on the specified inhomogeneous complexes.

proof.text: The open right cosets $Hx$ cover compact $G$ and are disjoint, so a finite subcover contains all of them. Fix a finite transversal $S$ for $H\backslash G$, containing $1$ for $H$, so $|S|=[G:H]$. Every coset is clopen because its complement is a union of the other open cosets. Write $x=r(x)s(x)$ uniquely with $r(x)\in H$, $s(x)\in S$. On $Hs$ the map $r$ is $x\mapsto xs^{-1}$, continuous as an $H$-valued map with the subspace topology. Gluing on the open cosets makes $r:G\to H$ continuous. Uniqueness gives $r(hx)=h r(x)$ for $h\in H$, and $r|_H=\mathrm{id}$.

proof.text:
For $f\in B_H^n$ put $\widetilde f(x_0,\ldots,x_n)=f(r(x_0),\ldots,r(x_n))$. This is continuous and $H$-equivariant by the preceding identities. Define
$$(T_nf)(x_0,\ldots,x_n)=\sum_{s\in S}s^{-1}\widetilde f(sx_0,\ldots,sx_n).$$
The finite sum is continuous and $E$-linear in $f$. To check $G$-equivariance, fix $a\in G$. For each $s$, write $sa=h u$ with $h\in H$, $u\in S$. Right multiplication by $a$ permutes $H\backslash G$, so $s\mapsto u$ is a permutation of $S$. The summand evaluated on $a x$ equals $s^{-1}h\widetilde f(ux)=a u^{-1}\widetilde f(ux)$. Summing gives $(T_nf)(a x)=a(T_nf)(x)$, as required.

proof.text:
Each substitution $(x_j)\mapsto(r(sx_j))$ commutes with deleting any coordinate. Since the fixed action of $s^{-1}$ on $V$ is linear, the displayed finite sum therefore gives $\delta T_n=T_{n+1}\delta$. Thus $T$ is a cochain map. For $F\in B_G^n$ define continuous maps $a_s:G\to G$ by $a_s(x)=s^{-1}r(sx)$, with $H\subseteq G$ understood. $G$-equivariance of $F$ rewrites the composite as
$$(T_nR_nF)(x_0,\ldots,x_n)=\sum_{s\in S}F(a_s(x_0),\ldots,a_s(x_n)).$$
If $sa=h u$ as above, then $a_s(ax)=s^{-1}h r(ux)=a a_u(x)$. This identity will also make the summed homotopy equivariant.

proof.text:
Set $K_0=0$ and, for $n\geq1$, define
$$(K_nF)(x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1})=\sum_{s\in S}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}(-1)^iF(x_0,\ldots,x_i,a_s(x_i),\ldots,a_s(x_{n-1})).$$
Every tuple substitution is continuous; composition with $F$ and finite sums are continuous. The formula is $E$-linear in $F$. To check equivariance, replace every $x_j$ by $a x_j$ and use $a_s(ax_j)=a a_u(x_j)$ from step 4. Each argument of $F$ has a common left factor $a$, which comes outside by equivariance; the same permutation $s\mapsto u$ applies to every $i$. Hence $K_nF$ is $G$-equivariant and lies in $B_G^{n-1}$. No topology on the cochain vector spaces or closure operation has been used.

proof.text: Fix $s$ and a tuple $x=(x_0,\ldots,x_n)$. To expand $(\delta K_n+K_{n+1}\delta)F(x)$, let $P_i(x)=(x_0,\ldots,x_i,a_s(x_i),\ldots,a_s(x_n))$ for $0\leq i\leq n$, and let $\partial_j$ delete the $j$-th entry. The contribution from $K_{n+1}\delta$ is $\sum_{i,j}(-1)^{i+j}F(\partial_jP_i(x))$. If $j<i$, its tuple is $P_{i-1}(\partial_jx)$, whose term from $\delta K_n$ has sign $(-1)^{i-1+j}$, so they cancel. If $j>i+1$, its tuple is $P_i(\partial_{j-1}x)$, with opposite sign $(-1)^{i+j-1}$ in $\delta K_n$. These account for all the latter terms: one indexed by prism position $r$ and deleted original position $k$ pairs with $(i,j)=(r+1,k)$ if $k\leq r$, and $(i,j)=(r,k+1)$ if $k>r$. This is an explicit cancellation of finite sums, for this very homotopy.

proof.text: The remaining faces in step 6 are $j=i$ and $j=i+1$. Put $A_i=(x_0,\ldots,x_{i-1},a_s(x_i),\ldots,a_s(x_n))$ for $0\leq i\leq n+1$, allowing empty end blocks. They contribute $F(A_i)-F(A_{i+1})$, since their signs are $(-1)^{2i}=1$ and $(-1)^{2i+1}=-1$. Summing over $i$ telescopes to $F(a_s(x_0),\ldots,a_s(x_n))-F(x_0,\ldots,x_n)$. Summing over $s$ and using step 4 proves $\delta K_n+K_{n+1}\delta=T_nR_n-|S|\,\mathrm{id}$ for $n\geq1$. For $n=0$, $K_0=0$ and directly $K_1\delta F(x_0)=\sum_s(\delta F)(x_0,a_s(x_0))=\sum_s(F(a_s(x_0))-F(x_0))$, the same identity. Thus the bottom degree is included, and the maps vanish in negative degrees.

proof.text: On the complexes in the item take $\mathrm{cor}=\Phi_G T\Psi_H$ and $k_n=\Phi_{G,n-1}K_n\Psi_{G,n}$ for $n\geq1$, with $k_0=0$. The cochain identities and restriction compatibility in [lem-sfb-topological-homogeneous-cochain-coordinates] give $d k+k d=\mathrm{cor}\,\mathrm{res}-[G:H]\,\mathrm{id}$ by substituting the identity of step 7. All maps are linear and have values in continuous functions by that node and steps 3 and 5. This is an actual cochain homotopy in abstract vector spaces, before taking any cohomology.

proof.text: Let $b:V\to W$ be continuous, $E$-linear and $G$-equivariant. It commutes with the group actions, the finite sums and the tuple substitutions in $T$ and $K$, hence $bT_V=T_W b$ and $bK_V=K_W b$. The coordinate isomorphisms commute with $b$ by [lem-sfb-topological-homogeneous-cochain-coordinates], so the same equalities hold for $\mathrm{cor}$ and $k$. For a $G$-stable coefficient subspace $U\subseteq V$ with its subspace topology, apply the same formulas to $U$: the restricted action is continuous since the ambient action is continuous and has values in $U$, and its inclusion is continuous and equivariant. The inclusion equalities prove the asserted preservation, in particular when $U$ is closed. Only finite sums and compositions of continuous maps occurred, so none of completeness, local compactness or discreteness of $V$ is required.
